messages:
Maria: ok this is my peak WFH hack — shoved an old cable modem into a mini-fridge because it kept thermal-throttling during calls. box fan + PVC ducting to vent hot air. :grimacing:
Devon: 😂 wow. how hot was it getting?
Maria: around 55°C under load. fridge dropped it to ~32°C but had to disable the compressor cycle with a foam wedge, so fan + powerbank keeps airflow during defrost. engineering improv.
Sanjay: condensation is the scary bit. silica packs? moisture sensor? :sweat_drops:
Maria: silica packs stuffed in corners, taped seam, and a little baking-soda tray. night-mode temp check every hour. yes it's ridiculous.
Ava: that sounds like a segfault waiting to happen but also 10/10 creative. post pic pls :camera_with_flash:
Maria: posted image (img_2026_01_modem_fridge.jpg) 
Kai: love the ducting. did you 3D-print clips or is it duct-taped excellence?
Maria: duct tape and zip ties. no 3D printer this week. :stuck_out_tongue: 
Devon: PSA: if you're doing this, also lower transmit power on the modem or move it when streaming video — weird interference sometimes.
Sanjay: or cheap alternative: stick a small heatsink + a quiet USB fan on the modem. less condensation risk.
Maria: ordering heatsink+fan as we speak. this was emergency because ISP outage + repair ETA was 4 hrs out and I needed stable video for a demo.
ops-bot: Reminder: improvised hardware mods may void warranties. If this affects production, file a ticket with infra-team.
Ava: also vote: worst WFH hack you've used. one-word replies only.
Devon: tent
Sanjay: tripod
Kai: skillet
:shrug: Maria: hairdryer (short term)
Maria: poll open until EOD :timer_clock: — thanks for the tips, folks. will report back with a less-living-room-looking solution.
